Having dealt mostly with general enforcement and nonviolent crimes, she was understandably disturbed by the serial murders and other extreme crimes investigated by theBAU. The Heart: Takes up the role in J.J.'s absence, although it unfortunately ends up being to her detriment. Heroic BSoD: Her arc on the show is basically her descent into this. Morality Pet: Serves as one to remind the audience (and the team) that most people find what the BAU does to be a horrible job and cannot cope with the constant mental trauma. She Cleans Up Nicely: Not that Meta Golding was unattractive before, but going undercover in "52 Pickup" gives her a chance to look extremely pretty.

characters.name: Section Chief Mateo Cruz
characters.description: The newly instated Section Chief for the BAUafter Erin Strauss' deathfrom Season 9 onward. Cruz has previous history with JJ as a former task force member during an operation in the Middle East. Foil: He has none of Erin Strauss'Obstructive Bureaucrattendencies and treats the BAU with respect from day one. He's also a bit more active and joins the team on quite a few cases, even showing good combat expertise, unlike Strauss who only got involved ever so often and was never shown in active combat. Reasonable Authority Figure: After joining the BAU on a case and seeing firsthand how their methods work, he immediately realizes that the team works best when they're left on their own and simply stays out of their way. "Angels" reveals that Hotchner hears so little for him that he originally thought Cruz just wasn't reading his reports, but he was actually needed elsewhere by FBI higher-ups and trusted the BAU's success. That One Case: "200" reveals that the operation he participated with JJ in, the one in the Middle East, is the case that stayed the most with him. Operation "Classified" ended with one of their own revealed as a traitor and another FBI operative supposedly killed-in-action, and unfortunately both of these men come back later as part of the Regime Squad seeking to torture the two for information on the case and trying to set up a terrorist attack with lots of casualties in the USA. What Happened to the Mouse?: His last appearance in the series was in Season 10's "Beyond Borders", filling Jack Garrett in on the case at hand. He then never appears again for the remainder of the series, and is still to make a return even after Evolution.

characters.name: Linda Barnes
characters.description: The FBI Executive Assistant Director, formally introduced in Season 13 as a new supervisor to the BAU's actions. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She puts up a professional facade to hide the fact she's aspiring to become the new FBI Director, while unloading both her true intentions and her tendencies of control on the team with a condescending attitude. Control Freak: She operates and regulates teams based off a need to display power and control thanks to her position, aiming for efficiency and effectiveness rather than any sort of team dynamic because she wants to be Executive Director. Prentiss even says she boasts of her power not because she has none, but because she can't get enough of it. Drunk with Power: Simmons and Prentiss profiles Barnes as being obsessed with obtaining power. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: She mentions having a six year old son to Rossi.

characters.name: Deputy Director Douglas Bailey
characters.description: The ambitious new Deputy Director of the FBI who is introduced inEvolution. Cain and Abel:With his brother Peter. Douglas experiences difficulties with the BAU due to being a by-the-books hardass that's unwilling to damage his reputation, but overall is just desperately trying to do the right thing. On the other hand, Peter is a law-breakingConspiracy Theoristwho wants to depose the "deep state" that "abuses children", and his status as one of the Gold Star participants means he almost certainly has a body count even if it is not outright stated. It's Personal: He's generally a by-the-books bureaucrat, but changes his tune when it involves someone he knows.He inserted himself into the Sicarius investigation when a woman he dated became one of the victims. He claims to the BAU that he was asked to overlook this specific case, but they are able to see through his lies and find out that he wants to find the man that murdered his paramour.A much darker instance of this is eventually revealed to have occurred with the Gold Star case. His brother Peter was one of the test subjects of the Gold Star program, hence him urging FBI Director Madison to classify the case and keep the BAU's eyes off of it. When Voit reveals he knows about Gold Star, Bailey secretly attempts to bargain with Voit for information, but gets himself killed. He inserted himself into the Sicarius investigation when a woman he dated became one of the victims. He claims to the BAU that he was asked to overlook this specific case, but they are able to see through his lies and find out that he wants to find the man that murdered his paramour. A much darker instance of this is eventually revealed to have occurred with the Gold Star case. His brother Peter was one of the test subjects of the Gold Star program, hence him urging FBI Director Madison to classify the case and keep the BAU's eyes off of it. When Voit reveals he knows about Gold Star, Bailey secretly attempts to bargain with Voit for information, b

characters.name: John Blackwolf
characters.description: A teacher and sheriff from Terra Mesa, New Mexico, also a resident of the nearby Apache reserve, called in by the BAU and local police after a group ofUnSubsstarts killing people using Native-American rituals. Badass Native: He's an Apache member and a sheriff in Terra Mesa, and a really good one at that. Cool Teacher: Occasionally makes speeches and teaches children about Native-American culture at the local elementary school. He's also a sheriff and expert in combat. Deadpan Snarker: Pretty much engages inSnark-to-Snark Combatwith Hotch the moment they meet. Does Not Like Guns: Refuses to use guns in combat and is disapproving of their use by others.

characters.name: Captain Stan Gordinski
characters.description: A Chicago detective who once arrested BAU member Derek Morgan in his youth when he got involved in a fight with gang members. He's become a recurring presence in Morgan's life ever since. By Season 8, Gordinski has been promoted to Captain and his stance on Derek has softened significantly. The Atoner: In "Restoration", promising Morgan to help with the case and arrest theUnSubproperly. He also apologizes to him directly and later holds a press conference with him to discuss child molestation with the press. Broken Pedestal: When he learns that Carl Buford is the child rapist and murderer he's been looking for all those years, since Buford built a reputation as a respected community center owner. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He's a hard-ass policeman with a penchant for antagonizing people he's had minor encounters with, but he's ultimately just trying to do a good job. By Season 8, the "jerk" part hassignificantlysubsided.

characters.name: Sheriff Eva Ruiz
characters.description: A former Brooklyn homicide detective who semi-retired to be the sheriff of the border town of Terlingua, Texas, only to notice numerous undocumented immigrants going missing and ending up dead. She calls in the BAU for help despite her colleague's protests. All for Nothing: Boyd killed her in a futile attempt to try and frame the Lugo cartel further, as well as to try and get the BAU to chase them instead. Unfortunately for him, they had already figured out that theUnSubis a cop by that point. Do Not Go Gentle: Essentially cornered by Boyd, alone and without much of a fighting chance, she at least still tries to go out shooting at him. Unfortunately, he's just too quick on the draw. Due to the Dead: After Boyd is killed by the BAU, they mention that Ruiz' body was taken to her home in New York so she can receive a proper burial. One-Shot Character: The "Cop of the Week" for Season 5's "A Rite of Passage" alongside her partner Ronald Boyd... until Boyd turns out to be theUnSuband kills her.

characters.name: Matt Spicer
characters.description: A California detective investigating the Prince of Darkness killings, having called the BAU to help with the proceedings. His own involvement in the case is bigger than he realizes. Heroic Sacrifice: Lets himself be killed by Billy Flynn so his daughter will survive. Unfortunately,he never planned to kill her anyway. It's Personal: The Prince of Darkness case, since it's his biggest unsolved case to that point and, as it turns out, the killer murdered his own parents when he was younger. You Owe Me: Billy Flynn started killing in California again because he was building up to Matt's family, since he feels responsible for Spicer's rise in the ranks after letting him live.

characters.name: Rebecca Wilson
characters.description: A prosecutor from the Department of Justice that assists the BAU inEvolution. Fall Guy: The Attorney General sets up Rebecca to be oneshould Voit's family and Rossi die trying to keep knowledge of Gold Star contained. Fire-Forged Friends: At the beginning ofEvolution, Rebecca is dating Tara Lewis, having started a relationship after encountering each other at an Al-Anon meetup. It eventually goes south after Lewis urges her to withdraw the case that launched her career so the BAU may continue their investigation into Sicarius. Their friendship stays cold until Rebecca has to supervise a case that involves Tara having to deactivate a live bomb, with the stress that Rebecca experiences urging her to get back together with Tara. Letting Her Hair Down: Rebecca's hair is usually a firm comb-over, but when off-the-clock at a party the BAU is hosting she has a smoother bob cut. Locked Out of the Loop:Played for Drama.Rebecca's knowledge of Gold Star urges Tara to press her for details about it, but she insists that she can't and won't talk about it, being doubly irritated with Tara considering they broke up. It turns out that she genuinely can't, because the only thing she ever knew about Gold Star before the BAU started investigating it was the name.

characters.name: Lila Archer
characters.description: A TV actress on the rise who's been targeted by a vicious stalker killing her potential rivals and even people she cares about. The BAU's investigation gets her interested in Reid. Damsel in Distress: At the end of the episode when Maggie Lowe holds her at gunpoint in her bedroom, requiring Reid to talk her down. Protectorate: Reid's, as he was assigned to keep her safe at her home after she previously showed an interest on him. He does end up having to save her when theUnSub, Lila's friend Maggie, sneaks into her home and threatens to kill Lila if her "affection" isn't returned. Romantic False Lead: Due to their careers and the risk involved in Reid's, he ultimately rejects her proposals to start dating and she moves on to focus on her acting.

characters.name: Evan Abby
characters.description: A former environmental lawyer who formed the Earth Defense Force to protest companies failing to clean up leaking chemical storage tanks, he is initially suspected of being theUnSubbehind a series of arson attacks on people his group named and shamed. Though cleared as a suspect, he and Hotch form a connection during the investigation. Animal Wrongs Group: Averted: theBAUinitially assume the Earth Defense Force to be one of these, but Abby asserts that they never went beyond political protests and campaigning, andthey certainly do not stoop to murder to make their point. Deadpan Snarker: Upon spotting Prentiss holding a camera she's been using to take surveillance photos of him, Abby snarks "Hope your pictures come out ok". Everyone Has Standards: He has no problem with naming and shaming people who break environmental laws online, but he is genuinely appalled when theBAUinform him an arsonistUnSubis exploiting his group to find victims among those he listed online, since he never advocated killing anyone to make his point.Vincent Styles:[about the victims]Why do you care? You didn't know them.Evan Abby:[outraged]NEITHER DID YOU!When Abby cannot bring himself to look at photos of the Unsub's victims, Gideon concludes he's innocent, as if he were the Unsub,he would not be able to look away. When Abby cannot bring himself to look at photos of the Unsub's victims, Gideon concludes he's innocent, as if he were the Unsub,he would not be able to look away.

characters.name: Nathan Harris
characters.description: An incidental character met by Reid in Season 2 during a case involving a vigilante-type spree killer. Harris is a mentally-disturbed young man who fantasizes about killing prostitutes, but who sought out Spencer to get help. Being Evil Sucks: He's essentially developing a type of psychopathy that involves sexual sadism, and this would usually mean he'd be just anotherUnSub... Except instead of giving into the urge to kill, he actively seeks out theBAUin order to get help, since he doesn't want to do it and it's greatly distressing him. Driven to Suicide: He's thankfully stopped by the prostitute he lured into a room with him when she calls Reid and helps him with his slit wrists. Misunderstood Loner with a Heart of Gold: A dark variation. He certainlywantsto be a better person despite his mother claiming he's already a nice guy, and he's actively trying to seek help for his condition, except his condition is psychopathy and he's fighting an urge to kill for pleasure, all while being accused of the spree killings taking place during the episode. Red Herring: He spends most of "Sex, Birth, Death" being accused of being theUnSubsince he tangentially fits the profile, and admitted to wanting to kill prostitutes just when the spree killings began. Except of course, he's not the killer, nor does he want to be one.The whole episode also teases that he might end up succumbing and kill someone, but when he finally does get the chance, he ends up trying to kill himself instead.

characters.name: Tracy Belle
characters.description: A recurring character in Season 2, Tracy was a little girl and one of Jeffrey Charles' intended victims before theBAUsaved her. Except a returning Frank Breitkopf targets her and other people saved by the team in order to kill them. Back for the Finale: Season 2's finale, that is. She's an intended victim of Frank Breitkopf's revenge against the team, having already been kidnapped by the time the team follows his trail to Virginia. Damsel in Distress: The poor girl can't catch a break. She was almost killed by one of her own classmates, and then a creepy old man kidnaps and tries to kill her just to mess with theBAU. Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: A blond-haired little girl and cute as a button.

characters.name: Carrie Ortiz
characters.description: A girl orphaned in Season 3, who catches Prentiss's attention. Sole Survivor: Carrie is the only survivor of the attack on the Ortiz family due to Ervin messing up the lethal injection on her. She suffers fromSurvivor Guiltas a result. Sympathy for the Devil: Once Carrie learns of Ervin's abuse, she is much more compassionate towards him despite him having attempted to kill her.

characters.name: Paul Davies (Dante)
characters.description: A goth rock musician with a wild lifestyle who becomes a suspect during Season 5's "The Performer" after his fans start showing up dead with his album's name carved on their bodies. Foil: Lila Archer was a clean-cut actress still on the rise who loved what she did, but had her views rocked when theUnSubof her episode, her own best friend, killed people she cared about personally, yet Lila still insisted on continuing without fear. Dante's career, meanwhile, is at a low point by the time of his episode and, with his own agent orchestrating the death of his fans for the sake of profit, it's implied that he plans on retiring, or at least restarting his image and approach to music. Goth: A goth rock musician whose stage persona is a "vampire lord", with his fangirls as his "legion". This is downplayed, however, in that Paul Davies is seemingly tired of his persona and the lifestyle it brought him. Jaded Professional: It's clear from his attitude that being surrounded by crazy fans and indulging in the "sex, drugs and rock'n'roll" life has ultimately left Davies jaded on the profession, having lost track of his original passion along the way. The fact that the recent string of deaths was orchestrated by his agent didn't help.

characters.name: Mr. and Mrs. Porter
characters.description: Owen's parents from Season 5'sExit Wounds. Abusive Parents: Mr. Porter abused his wife and son and made them cover it up. Domestic Abuse: Mr. Porter is loud with his wife, telling her to do everything he asks and was violent with her. Freudian Excuse Is No Excuse: Despite being in a loveless and abusive marriage, everyone points out Mrs. Porter was complicit in her son's crimes and made things worse. Hate Sink: Owen's father is portrayed as selfish and abusive. He never speaks in anything but a rude tone.

characters.name: Ellie Spicer
characters.description: An intended victim of the "Prince of Darkness" in Season 6, he took her in after murdering her entire family with the intention of molding her into a killer. Boyish Short Hair: Done by Billy so she'll look less like a girl, also to help change her appearance so she wouldn't be easy to spot. Broken Bird: Watched her family die before her eyes, then ended up kidnapped by the man responsible after he developed a disturbing interest in her. It's amazing how she actually ends up downplaying this trope by staying firmly against Billy Flynn the whole way through. Foil: To Tracy Belle from Season 2. Both were intended victims of dangerousUnSubswho were saved just in time by theBAU, but Tracy is a blond-hairedGirly Girland still has her family with her, while Ellie is a black-hairedTomboywho tragically lost most of hers and acts a lot more maturely than her age suggests. Important Haircut: Billy cuts her hair to make her look less like her description.

characters.name: Julio Ruiz
characters.description: An incidental character met in Season 6. Julio is an ex-gangster and Palo practitioner brought in as a suspect in Hollis Walker's murders. Awesomeness by Analysis: His eyes pretty much lock on to Reid the second they first see each other, and he immediately figures out he's suffering from headaches, as well as his overall personality, just by looking at him during interrogation. The man could easily be mistaken as a Palo counterpart to the BAU themselves from just how fast he can read people. Badass in Distress: He's taken hostage by Hollis Walker when his apprentice Elian is kidnapped and he goes looking for him. It was pretty much the first of two terrible ideas Walker would have that night. Holier than Thou: Distrusts police because of his upbringing and acts like they're merely pegging him for the criminal as an easy excuse, often citing his religion to distance himself from human cruelty. Thesecondhe hears that Elian might be the next victim, he drops it. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He's quiet and distrusting of cops because of his history, but he works at a community center helping people and his practice is always done to help the locals. He also volunteers to help the BAU and cites a short Mayombe prayer to protect Reid when they go after theUnSub.

characters.name: Sandra Madsen
characters.description: A narcissistic newswoman and director of Channel 3 News in Miami from Season 13. Her coverage of a child's near-death experience years before becomes the focus of the BAU's investigation when said child resurfaces as a dangerousUnSub. Composite Character: She has the same type of disturbing need for attention and glory as Agent Jill Morris from Season 3, but with the job of Morris' deceased best friend Katrina Townsley, a reporter. Foil: To Jeffrey Whitfield, theUnSub. Both crave attention from the media and both have an unethical approach to it, but even Sandra in her narcissism wouldn't resort to killing the way Jeffrey did. Ignored Aesop: The whole episode is a traumatic reminder towards Sandra of how dangerous her own need of attention is, especially when she's held hostage and almost killed for all the world to witness in a livestream set up by theUnSub... Except when he's arrested and Rossi confronts her, she's learnednothing, even expressing a sense ofthrillduring the hostage situation and feeling completely validated when the reporters outside the Channel 3 HQ want to talk to her next. That One Case: The carjacking case that traumatized Jeffrey Whitfield was both her biggest opportunity and a life-long waiting time bomb, having kickstarted her career as well as Jeffrey'sStart of Darkness. It was her interview that awakened hisAttention Whoretendencies and, unfortunately for the BAU, she's hell-bent on continuing her involvement years later.

characters.name: Tyler Green
characters.description: A former army specialist who was less-than-honorably discharged after posting the aftermath of drone strikes online. His sister Alison was murdered by Sicarius, the focal threat ofEvolution, and when the police couldn't find her he went on a crusade to find her murderer. Always Someone Better: Hatches a plan to lure Sicarius out into the open and catch him on camera, but Voit sees through it and just watches as Green is arrested. Dark and Troubled Past: Besides losing his sister, his work as a drone spotter was very traumatic as it taught him to be dispassionate about killing others, and the immense guilt led to him publishing the aftermath of his attacks on the internet. Rossi even calls it "serial killer training". Drowning My Sorrows: Did this after getting discharged from the army, and afterhis sister's DNA is found in the second shipping container. Friend in the Black Market: Becomes one to the BAU in the second season ofEvolution, where they have him enlist the help of hismanyoff-the-books friends to get further into the case, or to track down people that don't want to be found.

characters.name: Sam Cooper
characters.description: Beware the Nice Ones: He's a generally kind and empathetic man, but there are a few hints that he's got a darker side, like when Beth has to stop him from strangling a particularly twistedUnSubto death with his bare hands. Cool Bike: Owns aHarley-DavidsonFXDBDyna Street Bob motorcyclethat he rides to work. We're shown him riding it at the beginning of "Lonely Heart". Mommy Had A Good Reason For Abandoning You: He likes to believe that his biological mother, whom he never met, gave him up to give him a chance at a better life. Mysterious Past: He's an old friend of Aaron Hotchner and David Rossi, has a history with Mick Rawson, left the BAU for a while and then rejoined it, is a Catholic priest and graduated from a seminary, and somehow got the authority to handpick a Red Cell team including a foreign national and an ex-con, two types of people usually not allowed to join the FBI. Ninja Pirate Zombie Robot: Catholic priest + martial arts training + Army Veteran + profiling skills.

characters.name: Beth Griffith
characters.description: Brutal Honesty: Has gotten her in trouble before. She has been kicked off several anti-terrorism teams for this. Cassandra Truth: They apparently would've caught the Beltway snipers a lot sooner if they had listened to her. No Social Skills: A milder example than most, but she's definitely socially awkward. Uncertain Doom: She is abducted in the final episode of the first season. Her fate was left hanging in the air when the show was canceled. When You Coming Home, Dad?: Both her parents were doctors and were constantly being called away, and she responded with increasing acts of rebellion up tosmashing her dad's pager in the garage.

characters.name: Mick Rawson
characters.description: Big Brother Instinct: Implied concerning his unseen little sister, Jenna. Handsome Lech: He's somewhere between this andChivalrous Pervert. In 1x04, he describes himself as a "serial dater" and has trouble remembering if his last night's date's name was "Lisa" or "Elise", but he also seems genuinely insulted at the accidental suggestion that he's just racking up notches on his bedpost.

characters.name: Jonathan "Prophet" Simms
characters.description: The Atoner: Wants to make up for murdering a child molester and admits to the unsub in "Two of a Kind" that the killing didn't make him feel any better and there's not a day that goes by that he doesn't regret doing it. Berserk Button: Hates child molesters and roughs one up in "Two of a Kind". Talking Down the Suicidal: Attempts this with the unsub in "Two of a Kind", but it doesn't work. Vigilante Execution: Prior to the series, he served six years for killing a child molester.

characters.name: GinaLaSalle
characters.description: Fair Cop: Part of her problem with her dad. He can only see her as "the pretty one". Military Brat: Child of a father in the military. She was even enrolled in West Point until she dropped out to join the FBI. "Well Done, Son" Guy: Her father doesn't have much faith in her career, and has apparently always viewed her as just "the pretty one".

characters.name: Jack Fickler
characters.description: It's Personal: His goddaughter is kidnapped in "Strays".

characters.name: Davis Scolfield
characters.description: The mentally unstable father of an African-American girl named Caroline. His wife left him due to his rage issues and tried to hide from him with Caroline, but eventually he tracked her down, kidnapped, and murdered her in frustration. Afterwards, still wanting to win the love and respect of a daughter, he started kidnapping little black girls as replacements so that he could play father for them. But, due to the girls being there against their will and Scolfield's unsettling personality, his attempts are always doomed to fail and he kills them when they do. My God, What Have I Done?: Seems to feel remorseful about the murders he commits. He marked his daughter's burial spot with a makeshift grave and he wrapped the two replacement girls in sheets and buried them with dolls. Offing the Offspring: Murdered his daughter in a fit of rage. Replacement Goldfish: His goal is to have a black girl he abducted serve as one for his deceased daughter, and invariably kills them when they disappoint him. Starter Villain: The very firstUnSubthe Red Cell faces in the series.

characters.name: Marcus Graham and Rachel Lancroft
characters.description: Cradling Your Kill: As mentioned below, Marcus loved watching his victims' bleed out. In the flashback to when he attacked the victim who survived, he stabbed her in the chest, pulled up a chair, held her hand, looked into her eyes, and kissed her. When he has Rachel start killing men, he makes her do this with them (sans the kiss) as well, but she's not as enthusiastic about it as him. Freudian Excuse: It's implied during his interrogation that Marcus' misogyny (and potentially his impotence) stems from mommy issues, while Rachel was sexually abused by her uncle and it made her an easy target for Marcus' manipulation. The Loins Sleep Tonight: Whileberating him, Beth Griffith suspects that Marcus is impotent due to the fact he never has sex with any of his fangirls and has to lie to them about not being allowed conjugal visits. Monster Fangirl: Rachel is one of Marcus' and she is so submissive to him that she's willing to kill people on his instruction. "Not So Different" Remark: Marcus insists that Cooper is just like him and pretends not to be. What he's referring to, is not exactly elaborated on.

characters.name: MargaretMcKenna
characters.description: Accidental Murder: While the first death attributed to her was a patient she gave a staph infection, his death wasn't intentional. Attention Whore: She hasMünchausen Syndrome by Proxyand tried several times in the past to get attention by giving patients staph infections, just so she could look like a hero by blowing the whistle on outbreaks. Creepy Monotone: During her murders, she speaks to victims like a doctor instructing a patient through a procedure. Theme Serial Killer: Models her murders after the Three Wise Monkeys."See No Evil", cuts out the victim's eyes and leaves them in a newspaper vending machine a day later."Hear No Evil", shoves an ice pick into the victim's ear."Speak No Evil", attempts to cut off the victim's tongue. "See No Evil", cuts out the victim's eyes and leaves them in a newspaper vending machine a day later.

characters.name: Jason Wheeler
characters.description: Cold Sniper: He has excellent marksmanship and he kills most of his victims withPretty Little Headshots. The only exception was his father, whom he killed in a fit of rage. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: Potentially with his sister, Amy. Prior to preparing for his endgame, he tells her that he loves her and leaves a suicide note in his shed addressed to her. Of course, given that he planned to massacre a bunch of people in her presence, how much he means it, is up for debate. Patricide: He has great marksmanship skill, but when he tries to join the Armed Forces or work for military contractors, his father wrote to them warning them that his son had rage issues and unstable behavior. Proving his dad right, Wheeler right became enraged and killed his father. Pretty Little Headshots: How he kills. Psychopathic Manchild: He's a grown man with the emotional maturity of a ten year old and a hugeLack of Empathyfor others. His whole reason for the murders is to practice up for a massacre of his dad's old army buddies out of spite for the elder Wheeler not letting him join the army.

characters.name: William Meeks
characters.description: Mad Bomber: Blows up a school and attempts to blow up a school bus and a hospital to spare his sons and many kids from what he believes is a doomed future. My God, What Have I Done?: As he's being arrested, he says he regrets bringing his sons into the world.Meeks:It was unfair of me to ever bring them into this world. Offing the Offspring: His goal is to kill his three sons in bombings while also blowing up as many people as possible, as he believes they'll be better off in Heaven. Villain of the Week: Of "Here is the Fire". Would Hurt a Child: His sons are all minors and he attempts to kill them with pipe bombs planted in their backpacks. Not to mention, all the kids he killed and injured in the school bombing, and the potential victims he could've killed in the attempted bombings of the school bus and hospital.

characters.name: Michael Vinoda
characters.description: Forced to Watch: A bizarre example. He forces his sister to watch him hang his victims because he thinks she wants to see it. The thing is, she's already dead and his troubled mind is just imagining her as alive, so he's just making a corpse watch.Michael:WATCH! Hanging Around: HisMOis to place his victims on a stool, put a hangman's noose around their necks, and kick the stool out from under them. This is because he's replicating how his sister ended her life and going further with it, Michael uses the same stool that she stood on. Parental Abandonment: His mother left and his father, not wanting to deal with the responsibility of raising two kids with mental issues on his own, decided to put both him and his sister in foster care. Sinister Suffocation: The victims don't die from a broken neck, they suffocate from the strangulation and judging by Beth Griffith's words, it's not a very pleasant death."Face bloats from constriction, body hemorrhage, petechia pops in the eyes, these men were in agony." Through the Eyes of Madness: Up until the reveal that she's already dead, we see his sister as Michael is seeing her.

characters.name: The Indianapolis Unsub
characters.description: Cold-Blooded Torture: What he does to his victims isbrutaleven byCriminal Mindsstandards. He puts wire tourniquets around their arms and legs so that their circulation is cut off and they don't bleed out when he dismembers them limb by limb with a bandsaw. Not to mention, he doesn't just do it in one sitting, he does it over the course of several hours, taking breaks in between each cut until the women are fully limbless. After that, he finishes them off by cutting their heads off with the same saw. Creepy Souvenir: Keeps his victims' severed heads. No Name Given: We never learn his name and he's just credited as "Unsub". Villain of the Week: Of "Jane".

characters.name: Leonard Keane
characters.description: Batter Up!: Beats men to death with his son's aluminum baseball bat. My God, What Have I Done?: Feels remorse for his fourth murder when the victim's mom calls her son's cellphone. Also, later starts to adopt the belief that what everyone said about him was true: that he was responsible for what his son became. Spree Killer: Kills three men in one night and two others the next day. Sympathetic Murderer: He was a completely innocent man who had his life ruined by the actions of his son, not only being harassed by a man intent on destroying him, but also dealing with the threat of his wife being kicked out of the hospital (which could potentially kill her) due to not being able to pay the fees, and being ostracized by his co-workers to the point it was effecting his job. Thanatos Gambit: His endgame was toMercy Killhis wife and ruin the life of the man harassing him by provoking the latter into shooting him.

characters.name: Trevor and Deirdre Norris
characters.description: Abusive Parents: Deirdre molested Trevor throughout his childhood. Freudian Excuse: Trevor targets and kills mothers because he sees them as surrogates for Deirdre, who has been molesting him and controlling him for most of his life. Villain of the Week: Of "Smother".

characters.name: Veronica Day
characters.description: Catchphrase: "The time is now." Clear My Name: The reason she's trying to get her case looked at again is because the only murder she was ever convicted of was her mom's. The issue is, that she's actually innocent and hates being blamed for it. Couldn't Find a Pen: Part of her signature was making her accomplices write "The Time is Now" in their parents' blood. Green-Eyed Monster: Admits the reason she committed her crimes was because she was jealous of happy families, which she never had. Manipulative Bastard: HerMOwas convincing dark-haired teenage boys to shoot their parents with a shotgun.

characters.name: Ben Armus
characters.description: Broken-Window Warning: As part of a plan to make his father think he's being targeted by an accomplice of Veronica Day, he smashes a window on his car and writes "The Time is Now" on the hood. Couldn't Find a Pen: Uses pig's blood to write "The Time is Now" on his dad's car and the wall in his parents' room. Hidden Villain: "Villain" is pushing it, as he's just a kid acting out, but the Red Cell team do start investigating his crimes after believing they could be threats from a fan/accomplice of Veronica Day; the woman that Ben's dad is prosecuting. By the end, Beth Griffith figures out that it was him when she finds a receipt for the pig's blood he's been using to write the messages. Villain of the Week: Shares this role with Veronica Day in "The Time is Now", though they're not working together.

characters.name: The DC Traffickers
characters.description: Cigarette Burns: Page tortures his accomplices by burning a mark onto the backs of their knees for each day he has them. In Carp's case, she had twenty-one burns. Human Traffickers: Luca is the leader of a ring that sells women into sex slavery. He enlists in the help of Page by supplying him with accomplices to lure in new victims. While working with him, Page is allowed to brutalize and kill his accomplices if they anger him, as long as he prepares the other women for auction. Mugging the Monster: Justified. Their latest abductee ends up being the daughter of a prominent judge and the goddaughter of the director of theFBI. Needless to say, when Page and Luca are both apprehended, they are reminded of how much worse said director can make their lives and they end up caving. Stocking Mask: Page wears one that covers the upper half of his face for most of his screen time as the unsub. There's No Kill like Overkill: When Page kills Carp, he stabs herthirty timesand twists the knife with most of the stabs to make her suffer.

characters.name: Kelvin Cornwell
characters.description: Abusive Parents: Prior to the episode, he disfigured his daughter by pressing her face against a hot stove. Not to mention, all the emotional abuse he inflicts on her by keeping her isolated, forcing her to wear a mask, and convincing her that her face is still in need of fixing (when it's already healed). The Atoner: Wants to make up for hurting his daughter, but his guilt and narcissism keep him from realizing it's unnecessary, as her face healed on its own. Villain of the Week: Of "The Girl in the Blue Mask".

characters.name: Richard Stahl
characters.description: Death Seeker: When he and Rawlins kidnap Beth Griffith in order to force Sam Cooper to murder someone, he's the "someone" and pleads with Cooper to end his suffering."I just want this to be over." The Dragon: To Rawlins. Freudian Excuse: Witnessed his parents' murders at seven years old and developed a masochistic obsession with death believing he deserved all kinds of pain. This made him an easy target for Rawlins. Self-Harm: He cut off two of his fingers when he was twelve years old. Sympathetic Villain, Despicable Villain: Might not seem like it at first, but when you learn his backstory and how he is a puppet of Rawlins, it becomes easier to feel bad for him. His boss, on the other hand is just a sadistic monster.

characters.name: Rawlins
characters.description: Final Boss: The final villain the team faces in the series. Hidden Villain: It's not known Rawlins is the mastermind until he kidnaps and reveals himself to Beth Griffith. Last-Name Basis: His first name is unknown. Sadistic Choice: What he does with his targets: he has Stahl abduct that person's loved one, gives the person a revolver, and tells them that they need to kill a random person and drop the weapon within a time limit, or else their loved one will be killed.

characters.name: Drew Leland
characters.description: Just Got Out of Jail: He was paroled four months prior to the episode. One-Shot Character: Only appears in "Two of a Kind". Would Hurt a Child: The crime he served time for was sexually assaulting a minor.

characters.name: Maya Hazel
characters.description: Attempted Suicide: Tried to kill herself with an overdose when Marcus broke it off with her, but it didn't work. She also tries it again via cutting her arm with a boxcutter when cornered by the Red Cell team, but they save her. Bullied into Depression: The reason she's so mentally unwell is due to the ridicule she received for her weight problems in childhood. She only improved herself for her boyfriend and the minute he dumped her, she attempted suicide. Formerly Fat: Spent most of her childhood obese due to a thyroid glandular deformity. When she met Marcus, he convinced her to work out and slim up for him. Red Herring: She is initially suspected of being Marcus' accomplice and this is not helped by her suspiciously watching the Red Cell team search through her shop before attempting to flee, but she is proven innocent after the agents learn that she was in therapy during the murders.

characters.name: David Henry
characters.description: One-Shot Character: Only appears in "Here is the Fire".

characters.name: Matthew Keane
characters.description: ASerial Killerthat murdered five people throughout 2006 and 2007 for unknown reasons. Asshole Victim: Considering that he killed five and indirectly ruined the lives of his parents as well, him getting murdered in prison was a deserving fate. One-Shot Character: Only appears in "Nighthawk". Posthumous Character: Died before the events of "Nighthawk", but can be seen in old interviews with his father. Used to Be a Sweet Kid: His father recalls a time when he, his wife, and Matthew helped nurse an injured nighthawk back to health.Leonard:He wasn't always bad.

characters.name: Peter Lidge
characters.description: One-Shot Character: Only appears throughout a couple brief moments in "The Time is Now", aside from theFlashbackCold Open. Self-Made Orphan: Murders his parents with a shotgun for Veronica.

characters.name: Gordon Ramirez
characters.description: A prosecutor that was responsible for convicting serial killer, Veronica Day. Miscarriage of Justice:  Downplayed. Back when prosecuting Veronica for the murder of her mother, he deliberately withheld the testimony of a witness that would've cleared her name due to believing it wasn't reliable. Of course, the formerwasstill a serial killer, it's just that her mother wasn't one of her victims.

characters.name: Emory Boyd
characters.description: Offscreen Moment of Awesome: Prior to the episode, he fought a bear with just a knife and survived. Of course, he got real messed up from the ordeal, but considering what bears can do to people, it's impressive that he even managed to walk away in one piece. One-Shot Character: Only appears in "The Girl in the Blue Mask".

characters.name: Dale Dixon
characters.description: Bad Liar: The Red Cell team see right through him when they come to ask him about the murder.Cooper:You think you're a good liar, Dale. You're not. Boom, Headshot!: How he kills Peter Warsaw. Moral Dilemma: He's forced to decide between shooting a random person or letting the kidnapper kill his son. He chooses the former. One-Shot Character: Only appears in "Death by a Thousand Cuts".

characters.name: Daniel Barnes
characters.description: Beard of Evil: Has subtle stubble and based on his record, he'sdefinitelyevil. Distinguishing Mark: Missing three fingers on his left hand. Off on a Technicality: According to Garcia, the case against him was dismissed for this reason. Posthumous Character: Died before the episode and is only seen in a photo. Prison Rape: His specialty.
